title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 2nd District

context.text: Incumbent Joe Wilson (R) won renomination in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with 74.2% of the vote.
Zyon Khalifa won the Democratic primary runoff on June 23, 2026 with 53.8% of the vote, defeating David Robinson II.

candidates.name: Joe Wilson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with 74.2% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2001); previously South Carolina State Senate (1984-2001)

summary.text: Joe Wilson is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in South Carolina's 2nd District, which he has represented since 2001. A Charleston native and attorney, he served in the Army Reserve and South Carolina Army National Guard, worked on the staffs of Sen. Strom Thurmond and Rep. Floyd Spence, and served 17 years in the state Senate. He serves on the House Armed Services, Foreign Affairs, and Education and the Workforce committees, and describes his priorities as a strong national defense, lower taxes and limited government spending.

background.text: Born in Charleston, South Carolina, and graduated from the High School of Charleston. Wikipedia gives his birth date as July 31, 1947.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Washington and Lee University (1969) and a law degree from the University of South Carolina (1972).

Served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1972 to 1975, then in the South Carolina Army National Guard. He retired as a colonel in the summer of 2003, having served as a Staff Judge Advocate with the 218th Mechanized Infantry Brigade, for 31 years of military service in total.

A real estate attorney, he was a founding partner of the West Columbia law firm Kirkland, Wilson, Moore, Taylor & Thomas. Earlier he worked on the staffs of Sen. Strom Thurmond and Rep. Floyd Spence and was Deputy General Counsel to Energy Secretary James Edwards in the Reagan administration.

Served in the South Carolina State Senate (District 23), 1984-2001, including as chairman of the Senate Transportation Committee, which his official biography describes as the first Republican chairman since Reconstruction.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2001 and has represented South Carolina's 2nd District since.

Serves on the House Armed Services Committee (Subcommittees on Readiness and Strategic Forces), the Foreign Affairs Committee (Subcommittees on Europe and on the Middle East and North Africa), and the Education and the Workforce Committee (Subcommittees on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions and on Higher Education and Workforce Development).

Chairs the U.S. Helsinki Commission and the Republican Policy Committee's National Security Taskforce, and formerly chaired the Republican Study Committee's National Security and Foreign Affairs Task Force (116th-118th Congresses), according to his official biography.
Won the June 9, 2026, Republican primary with 74.2% of the vote over Hamp Redmond and Sam Gibbons.
According to his official biography, he is married to Roxanne and they have four sons, all of whom have served in the U.S. military; his oldest son, Alan, is South Carolina's Attorney General.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services (Readiness and Strategic Forces subcommittees), the Committee on Education and the Workforce, and the Committee on Foreign Affairs (2025-2026 assignments).

candidates.name: Zyon Khalifa
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff (June 23, 2026) with 53.8% of the vote

summary.text: Zyon Khalifa is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 2nd District. A South Carolina native, Air Force veteran and recent law school graduate, he won the June 23, 2026, runoff to become the nominee. He says he is running on economic opportunity, affordability and infrastructure, healthcare access, and veterans' benefits.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is a South Carolina native who graduated from Silver Bluff High School. He told the Post and Courier he grew up in a household that sometimes lacked electricity and enough food.
Served in the U.S. Air Force from 2020 to 2025.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of South Carolina in 2023, where, according to the Post and Courier, he was an athlete, and a law degree from the Southern University Law Center in 2026.
Finished second in the June 9, 2026, Democratic primary with 34.1% behind David Robinson II (41.0%), then won the June 23 runoff with 53.8% of the vote.
Describes himself as a Gen Z candidate and "next-generation leader" focused on engaging voters who have historically been overlooked, particularly young people.

priorities.text: Expanding economic opportunity, supporting small businesses and workforce development, and improving infrastructure so families do not have to leave the district to succeed.
Improving healthcare access and affordability, especially in underserved areas.
Advancing data privacy protections and criminal justice reform focused on both public safety and rehabilitation.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to ensuring affordable, accessible healthcare for all, especially in underserved areas.
positions.quote: I am committed to ensuring affordable, accessible healthcare for all, especially in underserved areas.

candidates.name: Dayna Alane Smith

summary.text: Dayna Alane Smith is the Workers Party candidate on the November 3, 2026, general-election ballot for South Carolina's 2nd Congressional District. She ran in the 2018 special Democratic primary for South Carolina State Senate District 20. Little other public biographical information was found.

background.text: Ran in the August 14, 2018, special Democratic primary for South Carolina State Senate District 20, finishing second with 362 votes (11.0%) behind Dick Harpootlian (80.7%).
Listed by Ballotpedia as the Workers Party candidate in the 2026 general election; she had not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.
